definitions.explanation: An older male relative by marriage: one's spouse's older brother, or one's older sister's husband. Composed of 義 (here, 'by marriage') + 兄 (older brother). A formal term used in writing and official contexts.

examples.japanese: {義兄|ぎけい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{医者|いしゃ}→医者：02847_isha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{義兄|ぎけい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦スピーチ→スピーチ：03852_supiichi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{頼|たの}まれた→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I was asked by my brother-in-law to give a speech at the wedding.

examples.japanese: {義兄|ぎけい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{近|ちか}い→近い：00530_chikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦お{正月|しょうがつ}→お正月：05586_oshougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{会|あ}う→会う：00482_au⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{遅|おそ}く→遅い：00533_osoi⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{飲|の}み→飲む：00322_nomu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{話|はな}し{込|こ}む→話し込む：20658_hanashikomu⟧。
examples.english: My brother-in-law and I are close in age, so whenever we meet at New Year's we stay up late drinking and talking.

notes:
USAGE:
{義兄|ぎけい} is a formal, written term. In everyday conversation, people typically say お{義兄|にい}さん or ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{兄|あに}→兄：00570_ani⟧. The {義|ぎ} prefix indicates a family relationship by marriage rather than by blood. {義兄|ぎけい} can also mean an older stepbrother (through a parent's remarriage) or an older sworn brother, one bound by a pledge of brotherhood (see ⟦{義兄弟|ぎきょうだい}→義兄弟：15305_gikyoudai⟧).

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{義弟|ぎてい}→義弟：13981_gitei⟧ (younger brother-in-law)
- ⟦{義姉|ぎし}→義姉：17835_gishi⟧ (older sister-in-law)
- ⟦{義妹|ぎまい}→義妹：18404_gimai⟧ (younger sister-in-law)
- ⟦{義父|ぎふ}→義父：06725_gifu⟧ (father-in-law)
- ⟦{義母|ぎぼ}→義母：06724_gibo⟧ (mother-in-law)

The spoken form お{義兄|にい}さん uses the kun'yomi reading and is warmer and more familiar.
